item.title: PPP, PML-N continue war of words on eve of Muzaffarabad elections
item.description:
The PPP and the PML-N continued lambasting each other on Saturday, extending their rhetoric from the ongoing elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to the other party’s previous tenures in power.

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged as the winner in the elections in AJK’s Mirpur division. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling.

Political temperatures remain high as the second phase of AJK elections is set to be held tomorrow in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division. The third phase is scheduled for August 10 in all 12 refugee constituencies and 11 constituencies of Poonch division.

In the latest exchange, PML-N senior leader Rana Sanaullah remarked on President Asif Ali Zardari’s role as he responded to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections.

“If you call the votes secured by the prime minister votes of Forms-47, then on what forms has the president gotten votes on?” Sanaullah said.

On Wednesday, Bilawal had taken a direct jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.”

Sanaullah, also the prime minister’s aide on political affairs and a federal minister, was addressing a gathering in Jhelum Valley alongside Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam.

Sanaullah further said: “If you say to Mian Nawaz Sharif that he became the prime minister for the first time or every time through rigging, […] then remember, it is also discussed here that someone also became the prime minister for the first time after breaking apart the country.”

He was referring to PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became the president of Pakistan in December 1971 after the secession of Bangladesh (then-East Pakistan) following the 1970 elections.

In August 1973, Bhutto took the oath as the prime minister in 1973 under the new Constitution.

Sanaullah also took a jibe at Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whose recent remarks have sparked a fresh debate in political circles on the matter of creating new provinces.

Calling Naqvi a “blessed one” of President Zardari, the PML-N leader said the interior minister had “made the [political] journey of 30 years in three-and-a-half years”.

“You began from where and have now reached where, and now you realise that this system is completely dysfunctional.”

In his speech, Muqam criticised the PPP’s governance in Sindh, saying that no performance of the party could be seen.

He also said the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) — a scheme that the PPP often takes credit for launching — was not “anyone’s personal programme but the government’s”.

Earlier on Saturday, PPP leader Saeed Ghani alleged that the PML-N had never won a general election without rigging.

This followed a press briefing by Punjab’s education and sports ministers, where they said that the chief ministers of Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had nothing to show for their performance.

PML-N never won an election without rigging: Ghani

Addressing a press conference in Karachi, Ghani said, “The PPP did not secure power through rigging in any of the elections held till today.

“On the other hand, however many times the PML-N has secured power, it has not been without rigging.”

Ghani, also the Sindh labour minister, made the allegation as he responded to a PML-N member calling on the PPP to not “give lectures on democracy”.

“If you do not want to give the PPP the right to speak on democracy, then will you give it to Gen Musharraf or Gen Zia, or the leaders created by them?” he quipped, referring to the two former military dictators.

The PPP leader said he “did count the 1985 election”, alleging that PML-N supremo and ex-premier Nawaz Sharif “conspired” against ex-prime minister Mohammad Khan Junejo.

He further claimed that his party “became a target of rigging” in the 1988 and 1990 elections, which resulted in the PML-N winning. He went on to allege that the PPP was again “controlled and prevented from forming a government in Punjab” in 1993.

Ghani alleged that the PPP was restricted to “16-17 seats” in the 1997 general elections, when Nawaz’s PML-N again formed the government.

He contended that although the PPP secured power in 2008, the “PML-N was made to win seats, especially in Punjab, through rigging during Musharraf’s tenure”.

Ghani claimed that the PML-N was “made to win” the 2013 elections as well.

“Then the elections in 2024 [took place]. No matter how many times they say, everyone, even children, know that the PML-N was badly defeated in the elections,” he asserted.

The PPP leader alleged that Nawaz, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz “lost their own seats and then blame us”.

Ghani made the remarks after explaining the rationale for his party’s stances on new provinces in Sindh and Punjab, stressing that it was based on the wishes of the people.

He emphasised that the Constitution required any such move to be made through the elected representatives in the provincial assembly concerned.

He noted that the “people of Sindh, its representatives and its assembly say there is no need for further provinces in Sindh”.

On the other hand, Ghani pointed out, the Punjab Assembly and the Senate had passed resolutions over a decade ago calling for two new provinces in Punjab.

“If the people and the elected representatives of Sindh say that there is no need for any new province in Sindh, then no one in Punjab has the right to say whether there should be a new province in Sindh or not,” Ghani asserted.

He went on to stress that the PPP advocated for more provinces in Punjab as the “people of Punjab and their elected representatives” desired that.

The PPP leader emphasised that his party “represented” the citizens of each of the provinces when taking a stance for Sindh and Punjab.

At the outset of his press conference, Ghani also took exception to comments made by “two ministers”, saying it seemed that they “did not know anything about Sindh”.

“They are restricted within a circle called Maryam Nawaz. They only see and say what she tells them, shows them and explains to them,” he said in an apparent reference to the Punjab ministers.

item.title: Numbers of small loan defaulters surge by 2.4m in one year
item.description:
Alongside large clients, the number of small borrowers defaulting on loans is also steadily increasing in the banking sector, particularly CMSME and agricultural entrepreneurs, as well as housing and personal loan clients.

The number of defaulting borrowers with loans below Tk10 million has more than doubled over the past year, raising concerns over the deteriorating quality of retail lending.

According to Bangladesh Bank data, as of the end of March, the number of defaulted borrowers with loans under Tk 10 million rose to 4.543 million. This number was 2.163 million in March of last year. The figures were disclosed in the central bank's latest report.

The report says the sharp increase in small-loan defaults reflects a significant deterioration in the quality of retail credit.

Bangladesh Bank has identified the rising cost of living, increased household debt burdens, sluggish SME activities, and reduced repayment capacity in the agricultural and small business sectors as the primary reasons for this trend.

While large-value defaults cause greater financial losses, the rapid rise in defaults among small borrowers is an important warning signal for the overall financial sector, the central bank said.

Masrur Reaz, Chairman of the research organisation Policy Exchange, told Prothom Alo that the growing tendency of small borrowers to default is deeply concerning but not surprising.

He noted that the prolonged economic crisis and high inflation have reduced the financial repayment capacity of everyone, from salaried employees to small business owners, as the cost of living and utility expenses like electricity and fuel have surged.

According to the report, more than 34 per cent of total CMSME loans are now classified as defaulted. However, banks say it is difficult to generalise the overall trend in small-loan defaults across the sector.

Bangladesh Krishi Bank, which has the largest agricultural loan portfolio among state-owned and private banks, saw its number of defaulting borrowers decline from 2.4 million to 2 million over the past year.

Despite the improvement, 38 per cent of its total loan portfolio remains defaulted.

Mohammad Nurul Amin, Chairman of Krishi Bank, told Prothom Alo, "The government did not reimburse the amounts for the agricultural loans that had previously been written off. However, we have already received Tk 6 billion allocated for this latest loan waiver. At present, 38 per cent of our loan portfolio is classified as non-performing. We are making every possible effort to recover these loans and are strengthening the activities of our branch offices."

Default status by loan category

According to Bangladesh Bank, total outstanding bank loans stood at Tk17.84 trillion at the end of March, with the overall default loan ratio reaching 32.7 per cent.

Among all loan categories, loans of up to Tk10 million and loans exceeding Tk500 million account for a significant share of both defaulting borrowers and outstanding defaults.

Loans of up to Tk10 million totalled around Tk4.1 trillion, of which 15 per cent had become non-performing by the end of March.

Although the value-based default ratio remains comparatively low, the number of defaulting borrowers has increased from 2.16 million in March last year to 4.54 million this March.

Meanwhile, outstanding loans exceeding Tk500 million amounted to nearly Tk5.76 trillion, with more than 42.5 per cent classified as defaulted. The number of defaulting borrowers in this category rose from 1,478 to 2,035 over the year.

Asked about the situation, Md Altaf Hossain, Managing Director (Acting) of Islami Bank, told Prothom Alo, "If we exclude the loans of S. Alam Group, our defaulted loans are lower than the overall banking sector. Although the non-performing loan ratio across the entire sector is around 30 per cent, our bank's non-performing loan ratio is between 22 and 23 per cent. We are continuing our efforts to recover these loans or bring them back into regular repayment."

According to Bangladesh Bank, outstanding loans between Tk10 million and Tk100 million totalled around Tk3.61 trillion at the end of March, with more than 26.5 per cent classified as defaulted. The number of defaulting borrowers in this category increased from 25,477 to 28,501 over the year.

Default ratios in larger loan brackets were also high. Loans between Tk100 million and Tk200 million recorded a default ratio of 45 per cent, with the number of defaulting borrowers rising from 3,336 to 6,186. Loans between Tk200 million and Tk300 million had a default ratio of nearly 36 per cent, while the number of defaulting borrowers increased from 1,125 to 1,574.

For loans between Tk300 million and Tk400 million, the default ratio stood at nearly 39 per cent, with the number of defaulting borrowers increasing from 605 to 952. In the Tk400 million to Tk500 million category, the default ratio reached around 45 per cent, while the number of defaulting borrowers rose from 392 to 669.

Regarding the overall situation, Md Mazibur Rahman, Managing Director of Janata Bank, told Prothom Alo that alongside large loans, agricultural and SME sector loans are also beginning to deteriorate. Because of this, monitoring at the branch level has been intensified and efforts are underway to regularize these loans under the central bank's special policies.

Default status by sector

Bangladesh Bank data shows that as of the end of March, the trade and commerce sector leads in defaults. 32 per cent of total bank loans are in this sector, nearly 44 per cent of which are now defaulted. Additionally, approximately 32 per cent of industrial loans and 34 per cent of CMSME loans have defaulted. Within the CMSME sector, the cottage industry has the highest default rate at nearly 53 per cent, while the default rate for medium-sized loans in this sector is about 38 per cent.

Consumer loans account for approximately 9 per cent of total bank loans, with a default rate of 7 per cent. The construction sector holds about 7 per cent of total bank loans, with a default rate of nearly 30 per cent.

Furthermore, about 4.25 per cent of total bank loans have been disbursed to the agriculture, fisheries and forestry sectors, where the default rate stood at nearly 30 per cent at the end of March.

Kamrul Mehedi, Deputy Managing Director of City Bank, told Prothom Alo, "Of our Tk 55 billlion in SME loans, the defaulted amount is Tk 930 million, most of which deteriorated during the COVID period. If support is not extended to small entrepreneurs in time, they fall into crisis. This is primarily why the trend of defaulting on small loans is increasing across the entire sector."

Gor proposes Bangladesh join US-led Pax Silica initiative
item.description:
US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor has proposed that Bangladesh join the US-led Pax Silica initiative, saying the country has significant potential to become a partner in the global economic security alliance focused on artificial intelligence, semiconductors and critical mineral supply chains.
Gor made the remarks during a courtesy meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Saturday morning, in a warm and cordial atmosphere, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
During the meeting, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman highlighted Bangladesh’s strong interest in attracting investment in the information technology sector. Gor said Bangladesh has considerable potential in the sector and could participate in the Pax Silica initiative in the future.
Pax Silica is an international economic security alliance led by the US State Department, launched in December to strengthen global supply chains for artificial intelligence, semiconductors and critical minerals. Led by US Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg, the initiative aims to bring together partner countries to reduce technological dependencies.
Gor said the US government has strong confidence in Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership and noted that stability has returned to Bangladesh under his leadership.
He said the United States’ recent positive revision of its travel advisory for Bangladesh reflected that confidence and would send an important message to US investors that Bangladesh is ready for investment.
The meeting also discussed the Rohingya crisis. Gor shared his observations from his visit to Rohingya camps in Cox’s Bazar and praised the Bangladesh government and people for providing shelter and humanitarian assistance to the displaced Myanmar nationals.
Prime Minister Tarique expressed gratitude to the US government and people, noting that more than half of the international assistance for Rohingya refugees comes from the United States.
Gor stressed the need for a sustainable and political solution to the Rohingya crisis.
The two sides also agreed to work together to resume product testing activities in Bangladesh with support from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
The prime minister urged greater US investment in Bangladesh, particularly in storage facilities for soybean, cotton, wheat and other agricultural products. He said such investment would help build stronger and more competitive supply chains.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman attended the meeting along with Prime Minister’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam, Prime Minister’s Advisers Rehan Asif Asad and Mahdi Amin, Bangladesh Ambassador to Washington Tareq Mohammad, US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent Christensen, and senior officials from both sides.

item.title: US sends positive signal on investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Visiting US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor has said stability has returned to Bangladesh and also conveyed a positive message regarding investment in the country.

Sergio Gor met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's Office on Saturday morning. Details of the meeting were later disclosed in a press release issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the afternoon.

The Special Envoy stated that the US Government has strong confidence in the Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's leadership. He noted that stability has returned to Bangladesh under the Prime Minister's leadership. As an indication of this confidence, he said, the United States has made a positive revision to its existing travel advisory for Bangladesh. He added that this would send an important signal to U.S. investors that Bangladesh is now ready for investment.

The press release also said that the meeting, held in a cordial atmosphere, covered a range of issues, including Bangladesh–US relations, the Rohingya crisis, the activities of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and cooperation in the information technology sector.

The meeting also included discussions on the Rohingya crisis. The Special Envoy shared his observations from his visit to the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar the previous day. He highly praised the Government and people of Bangladesh for providing shelter to the Rohingya refugees and for continuing humanitarian assistance.

The Prime Minister noted that more than half of the international assistance provided for the Rohingya comes from the United States and expressed his gratitude to the U.S. Government and people for their support.

The Special Envoy emphasised the importance of achieving a sustainable and political solution to the Rohingya crisis.

The two sides also agreed to work together on the resumption of testing activities in Bangladesh in cooperation with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The Prime Minister invited greater US investment in Bangladesh. The Prime Minister also invited US investment in warehousing facilities for soybeans, cotton, wheat, and other agricultural commodities. He said that investment in these sectors would help establish a stronger and more competitive supply chain.

The Prime Minister also highlighted Bangladesh's strong interest in attracting investment in the information technology (IT) sector.

The Special Envoy observed that Bangladesh has significant potential in this sector and could, in the future, become a partner in the PAX Silica initiative.

According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that in December 2025, the United States launched the Pax Silica initiative, an international economic and security framework. The initiative's primary objective is to build secure and reliable global supply chains for artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and critical minerals.

Also present at the meeting were Foreign Affairs Minister Khalilur Rahman; Prime Minister's Adviser on Foreign Affairs, Humaiun Kobir; State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam; the Prime Minister's Advisers Rehan Asif Asad and Mahdi Amin; Bangladesh's Ambassador to Washington, Tarek Md Ariful Islam; US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent Christensen; and other senior officials.

item.title: Govt to test MR vaccine effectiveness nationwide
item.description:
The government will launch a nationwide serological study to determine whether children have developed adequate immunity after receiving the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine, as Bangladesh continues to battle a widespread measles outbreak.
Officials said the study will begin after the required immunoassay analyzer—currently being imported from abroad—arrives in the country.
According to government data, 118 children died from measles and measles-like symptoms in July following the launch of the special MR vaccination campaign. During the same period, 30,209 children were hospitalized, while nearly 1,000 new cases are being detected on average every day.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the special vaccination campaign began on April 5 in 30 upazilas and municipalities across 18 high-risk districts after the outbreak started in March. It was expanded to the two Dhaka city corporations, Barisal, and Mymensingh on April 8 before being rolled out nationwide on April 20.
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain said the country's measles situation has yet to come fully under control, adding that most current patients are either unvaccinated or suffering from malnutrition.
He also acknowledged discrepancies in the campaign's target population, saying the estimates provided by the World Health Organization (WHO) had left nearly 4.6 million children outside the vaccination drive.
The government had initially targeted 18 million children aged six to 59 months for the special MR campaign and reported achieving 103% coverage. By comparison, the National Vitamin A Campaign targeted 22.6 million children in the same age group, leaving a gap of about 4.6 million children between the two programs.
The minister said the government will review the estimates in a fresh meeting and plans to bring the excluded children under vaccination as quickly as possible.
Public health experts, however, cautioned that vaccination alone will not be enough to control the outbreak.
They said rapid case detection, isolation of infected children, stronger hospital preparedness, intensive surveillance in high-risk areas, and greater public awareness are equally important to curb community transmission.
According to the experts, coordinated public health interventions should have been implemented from the outset of the outbreak. Children with fever should be kept away from others, while hand hygiene, mask use where appropriate, and public awareness campaigns should be strengthened.
Vaccine expert Tajul Islam Bari said antibody levels should be measured after vaccination to determine whether children have developed adequate protection.
He said an antibody level of at least 120 IU/ml is generally considered protective, while children with lower levels may require revaccination. Conducting serological surveys in outbreak-prone areas would provide a clearer picture of the vaccine's effectiveness and whether additional doses are necessary.
Explaining why some children become infected before reaching the eligible vaccination age, Bari said malnutrition, maternal malnutrition, vitamin A deficiency, underlying illnesses, and inadequate breastfeeding all increase the risk of severe infection.
Public health expert Dr Mushtuq Husain said post-marketing surveillance following vaccination campaigns is an internationally recognized practice that helps assess how many people have developed immunity and how effectively a campaign has performed in the field.
He said Bangladesh now needs to complement vaccination efforts with a broader public health strategy to contain the outbreak.
Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR) acting director Dr Kazi Ahmed Zaki said the nationwide serological study would begin as soon as the imported immunoassay analyzer reaches Bangladesh.
"Since this equipment is not available in the country, it has to be imported. We expect it to arrive within this week. Once it does, we will begin the antibody-related research," he said.
The findings, he added, will show what proportion of children who received the MR vaccine have developed adequate immunity.

item.title: Gor wraps up Bangladesh visit pledging stronger strategic, economic ties
item.description:
US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Ambassador Sergio Gor on Saturday concluded his three-day maiden Bangladesh visit conveying Washington's commitment to deepen strategic and economic ties and continued support to resolve the Rohingya crisis.
"The visit highlighted the breadth and depth of the US-Bangladesh relationship," the US Embassy in Dhaka said in a statement issued after Gor concluded his visit from July 30 to August 1.
The tour featured his meetings with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman, alongside a visit to the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar, highlighting the broadening scope of Bangladesh-US engagement.
During the call on with the premier at the prime minister's office on Saturday morning, Gor discussed bilateral relations, trade, investment, regional cooperation and other issues of mutual interest.
Following the meeting, the US special envoy, who is also his country’s ambassador in New Delhi, said strengthening economic cooperation and the broader partnership with Bangladesh remained a priority for Washington.
"Today, I had the opportunity to discuss with the Honorable Prime Minister Tarique Rahman the great opportunities between the US and Bangladesh to enhance economic cooperation and strengthen our partnership," he said in a US Embassy disseminated statement.
It added: "This is a priority for the United States, and together we can achieve real success."
During the call on, Tarique Rahman sought continued US investment in Bangladesh, particularly in warehousing, soybean, cotton, wheat and the information technology sector, saying such investments would help build a stronger and more competitive supply chain.
They also discussed expanding cooperation through the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), with Gor assuring Bangladesh that Washington would work positively for US engagements through the DFC, formed during the Trump presidency in 2019.
The envoy also informed Bangladesh’s head of government that US investors in Dhaka were keen to organize a US Investors Summit in Bangladesh in near future and he was personally working to facilitate the initiative.
The proposed visit of a delegation from the US-Bangladesh Business Council next month also came up during the talks.
The meeting further discussed expanding cooperation with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), while Gor said the US regulating agency would resume inspection activities in Bangladesh.
He praised Tarique Rahman's leadership saying stability was returning to Bangladesh and the US decided to lower its travel advisory for Bangladesh from Level 3 to level 2.
The Level 3 of the US travel advisory asks visitors to “reconsider travel” while the Level 2 suggests them to “exercise increased caution”.
The US special envoy said the decision reflected growing US confidence in Bangladesh’s security environment which would send a positive signal to US investors.
Gor praised Bangladesh for hosting more than a million forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals and continuing humanitarian assistance.
"The United States has supported this camp and urges our partners around the world to increase their contributions," he said during his Cox’s Bazar visit.
He stressed the need for a swift, sustainable and political solution to the Rohingya crisis through coordinated efforts involving ASEAN, neighboring countries and other stakeholders. The Bangladesh premier expressed gratitude to Washington for providing more than half of the international humanitarian assistance for the Rohingyas.
Earlier on Thursday, Gor held talks with the foreign minister, who described bilateral relations as moving in a "very positive direction" and said both countries were keen to deepen cooperation in trade, investment, energy, migration and regional affairs.
"We had a very productive discussion. Bangladesh and the United States currently enjoy an excellent bilateral relationship, and we discussed how to take it forward," Khalilur Rahman said.
The discussions covered issues including trade, investment, energy cooperation, migration, the Rohingya crisis and Bangladesh's forthcoming presidency of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
Responding to questions after the meeting, the minister said there had been no discussion regarding Bangladesh's relations with China or India and rejected reports suggesting that Washington had proposed a humanitarian corridor into Myanmar.
The US Embassy said Gor's visit underscored the enduring partnership between the two countries and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to strengthen cooperation with Bangladesh across political, economic and regional spectrums.

item.title: The Democrats have one last chance to halt the erosion of US democracy – and it’s less than 100 days away | Timothy Garton Ash
item.description:
American democrats need a Hungarian-style landslide to overwhelm Trump’s attempts to rig November’s midterm elections

In these days of extreme weather events, it seems odd to say that the US needs a big landslide. But a landslide defeat for President Donald Trump in November’s midterm elections is exactly what is required if the country is to start reversing his deliberate and rapid erosion of its democracy.

The respected Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute at Gothenburg University argues that in 2025 the US saw one of the most rapid declines in liberal democracy on record. “Democracy in the USA,” says its Democracy Report 2026, “is now at its worst in 60 years.” As the imperial republic marks the 250th anniversary of its founding, the danger seen at the very beginning of its constitutional order by anti-federalists such as Patrick Henry – that of an overmighty president abusing his executive power in an attempt to become a new king – has come closer than ever before.

item.title: Police issue nationwide alert over potential attacks on police vehicles
item.description:
Police headquarters has issued a nationwide alert, warning that vehicles used by the police could become targets of attack. It has instructed all field-level units to strengthen security measures with immediate effect.

Police headquarters' operations control room issued the emergency directive in a message sent on Saturday.

Police defuse ‘pressure cooker’ bomb found in bag left at grocery shop in Ashulia

The message states, intelligence reports suggest that police vehicles, including jeeps, pick-up trucks and buses, could come under attack.

In light of this information, all units have been instructed to exercise the highest level of vigilance to ensure security.

Officers have also been instructed to park vehicles in secure locations whenever they need to stop while on duty.

The directive further instructs all units to enhance security for government vehicles kept at police stations, police lines, office compounds and other designated locations after duty hours.

Officers have been directed to conduct regular patrols, maintain appropriate surveillance and remain particularly vigilant in identifying suspicious individuals or objects.

They have also been instructed to report any suspicious activity immediately to the appropriate senior authorities.

Bomb recovered beneath Motijheel metro station

It is worth noting that on 24 July, authorities recovered a bomb concealed inside an umbrella beneath Motijheel metro rail station. The following day, a sack with an umbrella protruding from it was found outside Bangladesh Bank, triggering panic all over.

Most recently, on Saturday afternoon, a suspicious bag was spotted on the second floor of Mirpur-10 metro rail station, while at around the same time another suspicious sack was found beside a pillar on the ground floor of Farmgate metro rail station.

Police were notified amid concerns that the bag and sack might contain explosives. However, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Bomb Disposal and Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit examined both items and confirmed that they contained no explosive materials.

Two metro stations closed after ‘suspicious bags’ found

These incidents have caused public concern. Sources at Police Headquarters said the authorities issued the latest alert after taking these incidents into consideration.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, Police Headquarters spokesperson and Assistant Inspector General (AIG) AHM Shahadat Hossain said, "The police regularly issue various directives to ensure security. This message is part of that effort. We have issued these instructions to keep the police active and vigilant. There is no reason to be alarmed by these directives."

item.description:
The government has approved the import of green chillies, with imports set to begin from tomorrow, Monday. Agriculture Minister Mohammad Aminur Rashid announced this.

The announcement came during a visit to Shantinagar Kitchen Market in the capital today by Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Agriculture Minister Mohammad Aminur Rashid, and State Minister for Food Md Abdul Bari to monitor the prices of essential commodities.

Green chilli prices soar past Tk 300 again

Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Md Abdus Salam was also present there, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of Commerce.

Speaking to journalists after the visit, the agriculture minister said the government had taken swift measures to stabilise green chilli prices.

He said the existing import duty on green chillies was being reduced and import permission had been granted. Imports will begin from Monday, and he expressed hope that prices would fall to a reasonable level within two to five days.

At present, green chillies are selling for Tk 320 to Tk 380 per kilogram in markets across the capital. Two to three days ago, prices had climbed as high as Tk 400 per kilogram. The sharp increase has caused considerable hardship for consumers.

Green chili prices surge past Tk 200 per kg

Addressing journalists, he said, “Report objectively what you observe on the ground. That will help raise public awareness and reduce confusion. It will also prevent anyone from creating an artificial shortage or manipulating prices.”

Earlier in the day, the commerce and agriculture ministers, along with the state minister for food, attended a meeting at the Ministry of Commerce to review the overall market situation for essential food and agricultural commodities and determine the necessary course of action.

They later visited Shantinagar Kitchen Market to assess the situation firsthand.

item.title: Commerce minister, Myanmar ambassador discuss expanding trade, Rohingya repatriation
item.description:
Bangladesh and Myanmar have discussed expanding bilateral trade, resuming border trade, and accelerating the repatriation of Rohingya refugees.

The issues were raised during a meeting between Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir and Myanmar's Ambassador to Bangladesh, Kyaw Soe Moe, at the Secretariat on Sunday.

According to a press release issued by the Ministry of Commerce, the meeting also covered increasing bilateral imports and exports, establishing direct maritime connectivity, the import of liquefied natural gas (LNG), and opportunities to expand mutual investment.

The commerce minister said Bangladesh remains committed to further strengthening relations with its neighbouring countries on the basis of mutual respect, trust and economic cooperation.

Matters relating to trade, transport, investment and cross-border connectivity would be reviewed through the necessary inter-ministerial coordination, he added.

Khandaker Abdul Muktadir further noted that the geographical proximity of the two countries, coupled with their existing economic potential, provides ample scope for significantly expanding bilateral trade.

Myanmar's ambassador expressed support for the resumption of border trade, saying that reopening the long-suspended trade routes would benefit both businesses and the public in the two countries.

If necessary, he suggested, the initiative could initially be resumed on a limited scale.

The meeting also emphasised expanding trade in a range of promising products, including agricultural produce, fish and fisheries products, rice, pharmaceuticals and frozen food. Both sides also stressed the importance of strengthening direct business-to-business (B2B) engagement.

The issue of Rohingya repatriation also featured prominently in the discussions. The commerce minister underscored the need to create conditions conducive to the safe, voluntary, sustainable and dignified repatriation of the Rohingya refugees currently sheltering in Bangladesh. He said Bangladesh is seeking tangible progress on the issue.

In response, Myanmar's ambassador said the verification of the repatriation lists received by his government is under way. He added that the repatriation process would move forward once the security situation becomes favourable.

The two sides also agreed on several additional measures, including holding regular meetings of the Joint Committee, convening the next meeting in Bangladesh, and expediting the finalisation of the proposed agreement to establish direct maritime and shipping links between the two countries.

According to both sides, direct maritime connectivity would reduce transport costs and transit times while significantly boosting bilateral trade.

Also present at the meeting were Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan, Additional Secretary (FTA) Ayesha Akther, and Myat Lwin, Counsellor at the Embassy of Myanmar.

item.title: Bangladesh launches action plan to advance safe, orderly migration
item.description:
The government of Bangladesh, in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), officially launched the National Action Plan (NAP) 2026-2030 to implement the objectives of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) in Dhaka on Sunday.
The event was convened by the Co-Chairs of the Bangladesh Migration Compact Taskforce (BMCT) - the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, in coordination with IOM.
The European Union supported the development process of the NAP through the EU-funded Prottasha II project, implemented by IOM.
The event also included a debriefing on the outcomes of the International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) 2026, highlighting Bangladesh’s leadership and contributions to the global migration agenda.
The National Action Plan was approved by the Cabinet on May 21, 2026.
Mr Ariful Haque Choudhury, MP, minister, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, graced the occasion as the chief guest.
Shama Obaed Islam, MP, state minister, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, chaired the occasion.
Md Nurul Haque, MP, state minister, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment; Mahdi Amin, adviser to the prime minister, Ugochi Daniels, deputy director general for Operations of the International Organization for Migration, attended the event as special guests.
Asad Alam Siam, foreign secretary and Md Mokhtar Ahmed, secretary, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, as the Co-Chairs of the BMCT, delivered remarks on the NAP and their reflections on the 2026 IMRF.
The speakers, emphasizing sustained collaboration among government institutions, international partners, civil society, the private sector and migrants for the successful implementation of the NAP, underscored the Government’s commitment to ensuring that migration remains safe, orderly and regular while maximizing its contribution to national development and protecting the rights and dignity of Bangladeshi migrants.
The event also featured Bangladesh’s renewed commitments and pledges towards the implementation of the GCM, remarks from the civil society, and the official unveiling of the National Action Plan. Bangladesh’s GCM journey, achievements and challenges were showcased at the venue through a video documentary and a thematic exhibition.

item.title: Decades on from the US’s disastrous campaign in Afghanistan, Trump is making all the same mistakes | Simon Tisdall
item.description:
The president has blundered into a ‘forever war’ with Iran he can’t win, but refuses to end. Such hubris has a long history

It’s five years this month since the chaotic retreat of US forces from Kabul. The Nato-backed invasion and occupation of Afghanistan, launched after the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks on New York City and Washington DC, is now widely regarded as a failure. It cost the lives of more than 2,400 US and 450 British troops, and tens of thousands of civilians (the exact number is unknown). Although al-Qaida terrorists were routed, their Taliban hosts reimposed repressive, misogynistic Islamist rule after regaining power in 2021. Afghanistan became a byword for ill-considered western interventionism and nation-building. It was the archetypal “forever war”, a phrase first coined during Vietnam.

If this cautionary tale had any lasting value, it was as a deterrent to politicians and generals tempted to rashly embark on open-ended conflicts without just cause, defined, achievable aims, and an exit strategy. Dismayingly, the forever war lesson had to be learned all over again in Iraq, which the US and UK invaded in 2003 and departed, having caused huge harm for scant benefit, in 2011. “Never again!” was the passionate cry at the time and since. And yet, it seems, the same disastrous pattern is now repeating after Donald Trump’s incomprehensibly foolish decision to attack Iran. A war he termed a “little excursion” is entering its sixth month and has been escalating rapidly. It, too, has a forever feel.

item.title: How Israeli presence in Forest City exposes the Zionist-aligned underbelly of Malaysia
item.description:
How Israeli presence in Forest City exposes the Zionist-aligned underbelly of Malaysia

Submitted by Miriyam Ilavenil on Fri, 07/31/2026 - 09:12
The controversy has fuelled debate over the country's pro-Palestine policy and broader questions about Zionist control
People hold placards and Palestinian flags during a demonstration marking Al-Quds (Jerusalem) Day after Friday prayers in Kuala Lumpur, 13 March 2026 (Mohd Rasfan/AFP)
Off

On 15 July, Anwar Ibrahim, the prime minister of Malaysia, said authorities would deport any Israeli nationals found in the Southeast Asian country, while strongly expressing that Malaysia would "not compromise" on its immigration policies.

"If we find any Israeli, we will deport them immediately because we do not recognise Israel," the prime minister said, according to local media reports.

His comments came as officials investigated allegations that Israelis were involved in a private residential and technology community in the southern state of Johor.

Johor Chief Minister Dato Onn Hafiz Ghazi stated that at the state level, the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) and relevant agencies would re-examine the Network School's business regulations. 

He also called on the federal bodies of the Home Affairs, Immigration Department, Police and Customs Department to investigate the allegations of Israelis in the Network School. Malaysia's federal Home Affairs Ministry later that day ordered a probe.

After two rounds of investigations, the Immigration Department said there were no violations among the 379 foreign nationals it investigated at the Network School, adding that 19 individuals' movements could not be traced.

The Immigration Department's Director-General Dato Zakaria Shaaban said that these individuals could have entered or left the country illegally. He added that authorities are on the lookout for the untraced individuals.

Then, on 17 July, Ghazi issued several notices to the Network School after authorities found that one of the premises linked to the school was operating without a valid business licence.  

On 23 July, the United States summoned Malaysia's ambassador to the US, Tan Sri Muhammad Shahrul Ikram Yaakob, to explain the nation's position on Israel. The Malaysian government stated that it would not change its immigration stance towards Israel. 

Founder of the Network School, Balaji Srinivasan, announced on X that he wanted an audience with the prime minister to restore his confidence in Malaysia as an investable jurisdiction. 

Balaji Srinivasan: Venture capitalist and Zionist ally

Balaji Srinivasan, a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist and Stanford professor, publicised the Network State in 2022. 

Marketing it vaguely as a startup society focused on peace, Srinivasan proposed building a "startup country" from the internet up. 

The Network State describes the idea on its website as "crowdfunding territory" and "eventually gaining diplomatic recognition from pre-existing states".

Malaysia vows to deport Israelis found in digital nomads community
Read More »

The website calls this new state a composition of an "ethnic diaspora" in which emigrants are connected with "the motherland" and come together in person to build dwellings and structures.

"In a sense, you can think of each physical outpost of this digital community as a cloud embassy," it says, adding that "recruits can visit either the virtual or physical parts of a network state, beta test it, and decide to leave or stay".

Along with Srinivasan, the Network State is financed by tech entrepreneurs Peter Thiel, Marc Andreessen, Joe Lonsdale, Patri Friedman, as well as crypto firms like Coinbase and Praxis.

Peter Thiel's Palantir has invested in Israeli military and surveillance startups accused of providing technological support to Israeli intelligence in the Palestinian genocide.

Praxis, a company funded by Marc Andreessen, Sam Altman and Peter Thiel, has proposed building a tech-owned city on Greenland after US President Donald Trump's repeated threats to take the territory by force. Trump has also shared the intent to build a Trump luxury resort in Gaza.

Critics argue that the Network State model resembles historical settler projects because it envisions digitally organised communities purchasing or controlling physical land.

Some scholars have also pointed to Srinivasan's frequent references to Israel as an example of successful nation-building, arguing that his writings draw inspiration from Israel's state-building experience.

In 2024, centring the pitch around proximity to Singapore, Srinivasan formed the Network School in Malaysia's Forest City, in the southern state of Johor.

Making of Forest City: Fisherfolk and reclaimed land 

The project's location in Malaysia's Forest City in Johor has added another layer of complexity. In a recent video podcast, Srinivasan alludes to the Network School being born out of "nothing into something". 

The "nothing" on which the multibillion-dollar development is built is termed "reclaimed" land in Johor and has faced criticism for its environmental impact on coastal ecosystems and local fishing communities.

Forest City is a joint venture between China's Country Garden Group and Malaysian private company Iskandar Esplanade Danga 88 Sdn Bhd (EDBS), whose shareholders include Johor's Sultan Ibrahim and interests linked to the ruling political party, United Malays National Organisation. 

Palestinian engineer 'killed by Mossad' in Malaysia, says family
Read More »

Between July 2024 and June 2025, Malaysia attracted about $759m in data centre investments, with Johor emerging as a key hub alongside the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone. 

An extensive investigation by Mongabay revealed how a Chinese builder began construction in the Forest City without an environmental impact assessment, devastating local seagrass and sparking strong community criticism.

The project also saw massive sand dumping, which destroyed marine habitats and hundreds of hectares of traditional fishing grounds. 

Rights groups have previously raised concerns that most of Forest City's workforce comprised low-wage labourers from South Asia, especially Bangladesh. 

The project has drawn controversy again, after allegations circulated online that Israeli nationals were participating in the Network School. 

The dispute exposed contradictions between Malaysia's pro-Palestine foreign policy and its efforts to attract international technology investment, even as government officials have maintained that enforcement actions were based on regulatory compliance rather than political considerations.

Neocolonial Malaysia: US imperial base, pro-Zionist hub 

The developments surrounding the Network School have fuelled a wider debate over Malaysia's balancing of its support for the Palestinian cause and economic relationship with the United States and western capitals.

The country is shaped by a constitutional monarchy, where political and economic power is concentrated among the federal government, state authorities and royal institutions.

Israel condemns Malaysia's decision to bar its athletes from competing
Read More »

The Federation of Malaysia was violently formed in 1963 and has since come down heavily on the people's movement in Malaya (West Malaysia) and Borneo (East Malaysia), allowing projects like the Network State to be built without much public resistance.

In 2024, Malaysia allowed a subsidiary of BlackRock to join a consortium to take ownership of Malaysia Airports (MAHB), Khazanah Nasional and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), under the jurisdiction of the finance ministry led by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

Civil society organisations in the country called on Ibrahim to make "the right and conscionable decision" by excluding the "Zionist entity conducting a settler-colonial and racist genocide in Gaza". 

Local media reported that the administration "launched an aggressive media campaign to discredit critics of the plan". 

In April, several international defence companies with business relationships with the Israeli military participated in the Defence Services Asia (DSA) and National Security (Natsec) Asia 2026 exhibition in Kuala Lumpur.

Companies included Lockheed Martin, a US defence contractor that supplies aircraft and other military equipment to Israel, MBDA, a European missile manufacturer whose products have been exported to Israel, and Colt's Manufacturing, a US firearms producer whose weapons are used by the Israeli military. 

Malaysia police free Palestinian kidnapped by Mossad agents: Report
Read More »

Civil society members pointed to investment links between Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby and Caterpillar, whose bulldozers have been used by the Israeli military in demolitions in the occupied Palestinian territories.

They also cited the operations of Australian rare earths producer Lynas in Malaysia, arguing that rare earth minerals are used in global defence supply chains, including those serving Israel.

Malaysian ports have also been used to facilitate shipments linked to Israel's military supply chain during the ongoing genocide in Gaza, transporting $885 million in weapons to Israel between 2023 and 2025, Al Jazeera investigations have found. 

In 2025, Ibrahim welcomed Trump during the ASEAN Summit despite protests against his visit.

Police maintained tight security, while rights groups accused Malaysian authorities of detaining and intimidating pro-Palestine protesters during peaceful demonstrations.

While officials have maintained that the country cannot sever ties with every international company that has business links to Israel, the Network School controversy has exposed Malaysia's projection of a pro-Palestine foreign policy alongside its ambition to attract foreign technology investment.

Johor remains a key destination for data centres and AI investments as part of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.

Why remittance inflows stay below $3b for second straight month
item.description:
Remittance inflows declined again in July after falling in June, with expatriate Bangladeshis sending home nearly $2.86 billion during the month.

In June, remittances totalled $2.82 billion, according to data released on Sunday by Bangladesh Bank. The decline comes after six consecutive months in which monthly remittance inflows exceeded $3 billion.

The drop has raised concerns among many bankers, who note that remittances are one of Bangladesh’s largest sources of foreign currency.

They said remittance inflows had remained above $3 billion for six straight months despite no significant increase in overseas employment, making the recent decline a matter of concern.

Monthly inflows

According to Bangladesh Bank, expatriate Bangladeshis sent $2.859 billion in remittances in July, compared with $2.478 billion in the same month last year, marking a 15.4 per cent year-on-year increase.

The central bank’s data show remittance inflows reached $3.425 billion in May, $3.127 billion in April and nearly $3.75 billion in March. Before that, Bangladesh received $3.02 billion in February, $3.17 billion in January and $3.22 billion in December last year.

The economists said it is still unclear how severe the crisis could become. If the global situation worsens, it could increase pressure on both the country’s reserves and the exchange rate.

As a result, remittance inflows exceeded $3 billion every month from December through May. Islami Bank remained the largest remittance-collecting bank, followed by Bangladesh Krishi Bank.

Bangladesh faces heightened risks from energy dependence and remittance flows

Why the decline?

Meanwhile, the exchange rate of the US dollar has risen slightly in the domestic market. After Bangladesh Bank stepped up oversight of commercial banks that were purchasing remittance dollars at higher rates, remittance inflows began to slow, according to bank officials, who believe the tighter monitoring may have contributed to the decline.

At the same time, the Middle East crisis has pushed up the value of the US dollar in the remittance market. To prepare for possible economic shocks, eight leading economists recently advised Bangladesh Bank to preserve the country’s foreign exchange reserves.

62pc of remittances from just 5 countries

The economists said it is still unclear how severe the crisis could become. If the global situation worsens, it could increase pressure on both the country’s reserves and the exchange rate.

They recommended maintaining reserve levels and avoiding an immediate cut in the policy interest rate, arguing that interest rates could be lowered later to encourage investment once external pressures ease.

However, Bangladesh Bank reduced its policy interest rate last Thursday night, with the new rate taking effect from Sunday.

The government will observe a nationwide public holiday on August 5 to mark July Mass Uprising Day. The day was added to the official list of government holidays last year.
Government, semi-government and autonomous institutions will remain closed on the occasion.
However, officials and employees of essential and public service institutions will continue to perform their duties according to their designated duty rosters.
Essential services include hospitals and emergency healthcare, law enforcement agencies, Fire Service and Civil Defence, electricity, gas and water supply institutions, seaports and land ports, airports, Bangladesh Railway, road public transport, prisons, disaster management services and other essential government services.
According to the Ministry of Public Administration's 2026 government holiday calendar, August 5 falls on Wednesday. Government employees who take casual or optional leave on Thursday, August 6, will be able to enjoy a continuous 4-day break by combining it with the weekly holidays on Friday and Saturday.
Whether private sector banks, financial institutions, garment factories and other commercial establishments will remain closed on August 5 will be decided by the respective institutions in line with government directives and their own policies.
Last year, garment factories also observed a holiday on August 5. At the time, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said in a statement that the decision had been taken in solidarity with the government-declared public holiday and to pay tribute to those martyred on that day.

item.title: Pakistan: Suicide bomber kills 14 at anti-militancy protest
item.description:
A suicide bomber killed 14 people and injured dozens more in an attack targeting anti-militancy demonstrators in the city of Kabal in Pakistan’s northwestern Swat Valley
Five police officers were among those killed at the event, which was staged outside a local police station to protest growing militant violence in the region and the state’s inability to protect citizens.
Those gathered accused authorities of failing to act decisively against militants, saying residents want to live without fear after years of devastating violence
The area was the home of Nobel laureate Malala Yousafzai, who was shot there by a Taliban gunman in 2012.
Hundreds of people were at the rally and social media video footage showed a speaker mid-sentence when an explosion rocked the area and sparked panic among demonstrators.
“The suicide bomber blew himself up when asked for a search in front of the police station,” a local police official said
No group has claimed responsibility for the crime.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif both condemned the attack.
“Terrorists,” said Zardari, “will never succeed in their nefarious efforts to harm peace, national unity and the writ of the state.”
Pakistan has experienced a surge in militant attacks of late, with many targeting police and security forces.
The Swat Valley was a Taliban stronghold between 2007 and 2009, when Pakistan’s military drove the Islamists out and re-established government control over the area.
The religious militants have recently resurfaced, however, with the Pakistani Taliban, known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, being particularly active.
The TTP is separate from, but allied with, Afghanistan’s Taliban rulers and has been a source of tension between the neighboring countries.
Pakistan says the TTP and other militant groups are carrying out attacks in the country with the support of Afghanistan’s Taliban rulers and has promised to continue targeting the TTP and its support network.

item.title: Cabinet scraps essential drugs list and pricing method
item.description:
The Cabinet has approved a proposal to scrap the Essential Drugs List 2026 and the Drug Price Determination Method 2026.

The proposal was approved on Monday afternoon during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat.

A press release issued by the Cabinet Division following the meeting confirmed the decision.

According to the press release, the government remains committed to ensuring safe, effective, high-quality, and affordable medicines for the public.

It further said that the rationale behind scrapping the Essential Drugs List 2026 and the Drug Price Determination Method 2026 stems from a statutory requirement under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2023, which stipulates that the National Drug Advisory Council must be consulted prior to formulating the essential drugs list—a procedure that was not observed.

Formulated in January 2026 during the interim government’s tenure, the essential drugs list and pricing policy were drafted without consulting the National Drug Advisory Council.

A writ petition challenging their legal validity was subsequently filed in the High Court, where the matter currently remains sub judice.

Meanwhile, on 29 June, the National Drug Advisory Council was constituted in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2023. The Cabinet has also approved a proposal to include the Director General of health services in this advisory council.

However, despite the cancellation of this year’s essential drugs list and pricing policy, the essential drugs list formulated under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s 1994 order, along with the government pricing mechanism for those medicines, will remain in force as before.

A decision has been taken to update the essential drugs list. Drug prices will be determined in a manner that avoids placing an additional burden on the people while maintaining healthy competition in the market.

Zakir Hossain, former Secretary General of the Bangladesh Association of Pharmaceutical Industries (BAPI), welcomed the Cabinet’s decision.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he said, “The pharmaceutical industry had been facing a stagnant situation for nearly two years. The Cabinet’s decision will resolve this impasse and restore stability to the market. Industry owners have shown complete sincerity, and it is hoped that the prevailing legal complexities will now be resolved.”
